title: US Jury Convicts Huawei of Fraud and Trade Secret Theft, China Launches First Foreign Astronaut to Tiangong, and WHO Demands End to Cuba Fuel Blockade
subhead: A federal court in New York found Huawei guilty on ten of twelve criminal counts involving sanctions evasion and intellectual property theft, Beijing sent a Pakistani fighter pilot into orbit aboard Shenzhou-24, and UN agencies warned of dual humanitarian emergencies in fuel-starved Cuba and storm-hit Gaza.

sections.heading: US Federal Jury Convicts Huawei on Ten Criminal Counts After Eight-Year Legal Battle
sections.body:
CNBC and Deutsche Welle report that a federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei on 10 of 12 criminal counts, finding the company guilty of bank fraud, money laundering, obstruction of justice, and conspiracy to steal trade secrets from six US technology firms. Prosecutors argued that Huawei used a Hong Kong front company, Skycom, to mislead global banks into processing more than $100 million in transactions linked to Iran in violation of US sanctions, while running an internal bonus program that rewarded employees for obtaining confidential router source code and cellular antenna designs from American competitors.

The jury acquitted Huawei on the overarching racketeering conspiracy counts after weeks of deliberations. In a statement cited by Euronews, Huawei said the racketeering acquittal showed those allegations lacked factual foundation and pledged to appeal the remaining convictions, which trace back to indictments first unsealed during the first Trump administration eight years ago. In a separate US enforcement action reported by the Financial Times, fast-fashion retailer Shein agreed to pay $100 million to settle federal allegations that its suppliers mislabeled cotton harvested in China as American-grown.
sections.whyItMatters: Criminal bank fraud convictions expose Huawei to multibillion-dollar forfeiture penalties and secondary banking cutoffs across jurisdictions that clear dollar transactions, hardening the legal wall around Chinese telecom infrastructure in emerging markets.

sections.heading: China Launches Shenzhou-24 Carrying Pakistan's First Orbital Astronaut to Tiangong
sections.body:
TRT World, CBS News, and Anadolu Agency report that China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft atop a Long March-2F rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on Wednesday, sending three astronauts to the Tiangong orbital station. Among the crew is Pakistani Air Force fighter pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who becomes both Pakistan's first astronaut in orbit and the first foreign national ever to board China's permanently crewed space station.

The flight stems from a bilateral human spaceflight selection and training agreement signed between the China Manned Space Agency and Pakistan's Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, under which Pakistani candidates completed multi-year spacecraft systems and microgravity payload training alongside People's Liberation Army Astronaut Corps crews. During his rotation aboard Tiangong, Ali will conduct life-science, fluid-physics, and Earth-observation experiments submitted by Pakistani universities before returning to Earth aboard the command module.
sections.whyItMatters: Opening Tiangong to a Pakistani military pilot turns human spaceflight into a diplomatic instrument for Beijing, positioning China's orbital station as a practical alternative to the US-led Artemis coalition for partner states across Asia and the Middle East.

sections.heading: WHO Demands End to US Fuel Blockade on Cuba as Winter Storm Threatens 1.76 Million in Gaza
sections.body:
Al Jazeera reports that World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on Washington to lift its fuel blockade on Cuba, warning that acute diesel and fuel oil shortages are paralyzing hospital generators, cold-chain vaccine storage, and ambulance fleets across the island. The United Nations allocated $2 million in emergency funding for immunization supplies and critical medical equipment as Cuban health facilities curtail elective surgeries and dialysis sessions.

In Gaza, Anadolu Agency reports that local civil defense authorities warned an approaching cold front and torrential rainstorm threaten the lives of 1.76 million Palestinians sheltering in makeshift tents without heating or winterized cover, leaving thousands of infants at risk of hypothermia. TRT World adds that Amnesty International petitioned the International Criminal Court to investigate documented destruction of maternal clinics and fertility facilities in Gaza, while in the southern West Bank, local mayors warned that new Israeli military gates west of Hebron could sever 70,000 Palestinians from their agricultural land.
sections.whyItMatters: Simultaneous UN warnings over Cuba's energy-starved hospital grid and Gaza's exposed tent camps underscore how blockade regimes and infrastructure destruction turn seasonal weather and fuel logistics into mass-casualty public health crises.

sections.heading: Houthi Strike Injures Eleven at Saudi Sovereign Wealth Tower as Hormuz Drone Clashes Persist
sections.body:
CNBC and the Wall Street Journal report that a projectile launched by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement struck the flagship skyscraper of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) in Riyadh for the second time in six days, injuring 11 people after the earlier strike caused structural damage without casualties. Meanwhile, Anadolu Agency reports that Yemeni government forces claimed to have killed 27 Houthi fighters and downed a drone during ground offensives across Marib and Al-Jawf provinces.

Across the Gulf, Iranian state media cited by Bloomberg reported that Iran's armed forces shot down two US unmanned aircraft — identified by Tehran as a MQ-9 reaper and a LUCAS platform — on the eastern and western approaches to the Strait of Hormuz, while Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei declared Tehran determined to break the US naval blockade. CBS News separately reported that Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz accused Iran of pursuing chemical weapons capabilities and left open the option of preemptive strikes.
sections.whyItMatters: Repeated Houthi hits on Riyadh's premier financial landmark bring Gulf sovereign wealth centers directly into the crosshairs of regional escalation, testing Saudi Arabia's effort to insulate its economic diversification agenda from the US-Iran confrontation.

sections.heading: Israeli Opposition Chief Eisenkot Signs First Coalition Pact Amid Supreme Court Settler Rebuke
sections.body:
Al Jazeera and Le Monde report that former Israeli military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot secured his first formal coalition agreement in his bid to assemble an alternative governing bloc, signing a pact between his Yashar party and Avigdor Lieberman's Yisrael Beiteinu. Israel's public broadcaster KAN reported that Eisenkot also made headway in backchannel talks with ultra-Orthodox parties, though negotiations remain deadlocked over demands to halt military draft-evasion arrests, prompting Democrats party leader Yair Golan to briefly announce — and then delete — a suspension of alliance talks.

The coalition maneuvering coincided with a sharp institutional clash in Jerusalem reported by the Times of Israel, as Supreme Court President Isaac Amit publicly condemned escalating West Bank settler attacks against Palestinians as a threat to the state's legal order. Opposition lawmakers in Washington echoed the criticism, arguing that verbal condemnations without prosecutions have failed to deter organized violence around Hebron and Nablus.
sections.whyItMatters: Eisenkot's alliance with Lieberman creates the first structured parliamentary vehicle aimed at unseating Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, though the unresolved ultra-Orthodox conscription dispute remains the decisive arithmetic hurdle.

bottomLine: Washington's criminal conviction of Huawei and its tightening fuel blockade on Cuba reflect an intensifying reliance on extraterritorial legal and economic coercion, even as Beijing uses orbital diplomacy with Pakistan to widen its strategic partnerships. Meanwhile, the second Houthi strike on Riyadh's sovereign wealth tower within a week demonstrates that maritime containment in the Gulf is failing to prevent asymmetric spillover into regional capitals.
sources: CNBC, Deutsche Welle, Financial Times, Euronews, TRT World, CBS News, Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera, Wall Street Journal, Le Monde, Times of Israel, Bloomberg
